description: [Ghanaian Times] Africa's labour market is changing fast, but one question remains stubbornly relevant: who gets a fair chance at work? For millions of women, having a job does not always mean having decent work. Low pay, unsafe conditions, unpaid care responsibilities, weak social protection and limited representation continue to shape everyday working life.
title: Africa: Feminism As a Labour Instrument - Advancing Workers' Rights and Decent Work in Africa

description: [Ghanaian Times] Delegates from across universities in 17 African countries have converged in Accra for the fourth International Annual Conference of the Harakati Za Muungano Union for development and freedom.
title: Africa: Harakati Delegates Discuss African Integration in Accra

description: [Ghanaian Times] South Africa is asking several other African governments to reimburse it for the cost of sending tens of thousands of their citizens back home.
title: Africa: South Africa Seeks Reimbursement for Migrant Repatriations

description: [This Day] After Nigeria and South Africa were denied direct qualifications to next year's FIFA Women's World Cup to be hosted by Brazil, the Super Falcons and Banyana Banyana have another chance this evening to fight for the 'back door' tickets via the African playoff.
title: Africa: Super Falcons, S'africa's Banyana Banyana in World Cup Second Chance Blockbuster

description: [Bird Story Agency] Africa grows plenty of cotton. It just does not make much of it into clothes. A new $5 billion plan aims to change that, turning a scattered collection of cotton producers into a regional textile industry.
title: Africa: Inside The $5 Billion Plan To Keep Africa's Cotton Jobs In Africa

description: [ISS] Current geopolitical tensions could be catastrophic for climate action, especially Africa's renewable energy transition.
title: Africa: US-China Rivalry Puts Africa's Climate Diplomacy to the Test

description: [The Conversation Africa] For centuries, useful metals have been developed by starting with one core element and adding small amounts of other elements. Steel, for example, is composed primarily of iron; carbon is added in varied amounts to produce different grades of steel. Bronze is made up of copper and tin. These mixtures are known as alloys.
title: Africa: A New Class of Metals Could Transform Africa's Clean Energy Economy - Scientists Explain

description: [African Arguments] When pastoralists, researchers, policymakers and development practitioners gathered in Marsabit this year to mark the International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists (IYRP-2026), the conversations went far beyond livestock, drought or humanitarian aid. Convened by the Centre for Research and Development in Drylands (CRDD), the dialogue challenged a deeply rooted assumption that has shaped development policy for decades: that pastoralism is an outdated livelihood gradually being overtaken by modernity.
title: Africa: Walking With the Herd - Why Africa Must Rethink Its Oldest Economy

description: [African Arguments] In the period that followed decolonisation, Africa's development landscape continued to be shaped by Western partnerships. By the late 1990s and early 2000s, this Western-facing architecture took the form of policy conditionality, governance agendas and institutional reform attached to rotating credit agreements. This approach rested, at least in part, on a simple reality: countries in the Global South had limited alternatives for accessing large-scale development financing.
title: Africa: The Beijing of It All - Africa's Development Terms Are No Longer Written in Washington or Brussels

description: [IPS] Nairobi -- Campaigners say anti-rights movements are increasingly using family law to challenge women's rights to inheritance, property, divorce and child custody.
title: Africa: African Rights Advocates Coordinate Response to Family Law Backlash

description: [UN News] Cholera is spreading rapidly across West and Central Africa, with active outbreaks now in six countries and millions of children at growing risk, UN children's agency UNICEF has said.
title: Africa: Cholera Spreads Across Borders in West and Central Africa

title: Africa: Exclusive - What Nigerian Delegates, African Group of Negotiators Will Demand At COP17
